posts.author: Cristiano_Perrucci
posts.content_md:
Hi all,

a couple of nights ago, I tried to make a Denisyuk but... I've got a complete disaster. Just a barely image was visible in the deep fog on the MBDCG plate.

A Mitchelson interferometer were istalled during exposure, so the cause of failure wasn't setup movements.

I checked polarization finding a strange behaviour of a plano-convex lens: when light passes through the lens, polarizazion seems to be degraded.

Putting a second plano-convex lens face-to-face to the first, polarization is completely lost. 

What's happening?

Cheers,

Cristiano, IT

posts.author: Tony

Cristiano, IT

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
To check for bifringence place the lens in between two crossed polarizers. If you see colors it is changing the polarization of you laser.

Remember it does not just have to rotate the polarization it can also "retard" it making the beam elliptically polarized.

This may be of interest:

[http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polarization](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polarization)
